title: Silverpine retail — real workload SLA gap analysis and mitigation proposal
summary: Hands-on POC notes and analysis mapping Silverpine's production traces to our synthetic benchmark results. Objective: explain why synthetic microbenchmarks underestimated p95 tail and propose targeted mitigations (cache warmup, adaptive batching, model quantization tradeoffs) with cost impact and rollout plan.
scope: This document covers: (1) differences observed between synthetic load generator runs and sampled Silverpine production traces; (2) targeted experiments run in Redwood Dedicated staging cluster; (3) cost vs latency tradeoffs for candidate mitigations; (4) recommended short-term and medium-term actions for the customer and internal rollout playbook.
methodology:
- Data sources: 48-hour production trace (sampled requests, anonymized) provided by Silverpine; synthetic generator used: rdx-loadgen v2.3 with configurable prompt-length distribution; Dedicated staging fleet matching customer's target node type (A100-80GB equiv).
- Metrics captured: per-request latency (p50/p90/p95/p99), token throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates, cold-start counts, cold prefix length distribution.
- Runs: 8 scenarios (see experiments) each run for 30 minutes steady-state plus explicit cold-start sweeps. Empty-model-cache and cached-KV-state runs recorded.
experiments:
1) Baseline synthetic (paper) microbenchmark: fixed prompt length=64 tokens, concurrency=32, measured p95 ~ 120ms.
2) Production-trace replay: heterogenous prompt lengths [8, 32, 128, 512], bursty arrivals, measured p95 ~ 360ms.
3) KV-cache warmup: pre-populate cache using 10k recent prefixes -> p95 reduced to 210ms.
4) Adaptive batching: dynamic batch cap with latency SLO gates -> p95 ~ 240ms, throughput +18%.
5) Quantized model (8-bit) run: p95 improved to 180ms, generation quality manual A/B showed minor degradations for long-form prompts.
6) Hybrid routing: hot-path small-model for short prompts, big-model for long prompts -> p95 190ms, cost +6%.
7) Cold-start injection: measured cold vs warm p95 delta ~ +320ms for first request after idle >8s.
8) Cache pruning stress: degraded KV hit rate to 40% -> p95 returned to ~330ms.
results_summary: Key observation: synthetic microbenchmarks systematically under-accounted for variable prompt length, cold-start frequency, and KV-cache hit behavior. Production trace replay exposed longer tails driven by: (a) a 12% fraction of requests with prompt length >256 tokens; (b) frequent short-lived user sessions causing cache churn and cold-starters; (c) multi-step multi-turn sessions where KV cache warmup matters. Quantified impact: moving from synthetic to trace-replay increased p95 by ~200% (120ms -> 360ms). Warmup and model-routing mitigations can recover ~35-45% of the gap at modest incremental cost.
numeric_summary:
Selected numbers from representative runs (median of 3 runs):
- Synthetic baseline: p50 35ms, p95 120ms, throughput 420 tok/s, cost est $0.012/1k tokens.
- Trace replay baseline: p50 110ms, p95 360ms, throughput 320 tok/s, cost est $0.018/1k tokens.
- Warmup (10k prefixes): p50 65ms, p95 210ms, throughput 365 tok/s, cost est $0.021/1k tokens (+17% ops for warmup traffic).
- Adaptive batching: p50 50ms, p95 240ms, throughput 378 tok/s.
- 8-bit quantized: p50 30ms, p95 180ms, throughput 540 tok/s, model quality notes in linked_artifacts.
- Hybrid routing: p95 190ms, throughput 395 tok/s, estimated cost delta +6% vs trace baseline.
cost_estimate:
Assumptions: customer baseline monthly tokens=3B. Cost deltas extrapolated from per-token run estimates above.
- If Silverpine accepts warmup + adaptive batching: estimated incremental infra cost ~ +$18k/month (warmup prefill run cost amortized) but expected to lower user-observed p95 from 360ms to ~225ms.
- If moving to quantized models for all traffic: infra cost could drop by ~20% vs current Dedicated bill, but risk of subtle quality regressions on long-form prompts—recommend progressive rollout to 10% traffic.
- Hybrid routing yields best latency improvement at small net cost (~+6%), recommended as staging step.
recommendations:
Short-term (0-4 weeks):
- Implement KV-cache warmup as scheduled background job that replays top-N recent prefixes to keep hot-state populated (N=10k chosen empirically).
- Add adaptive batching with latency SLO gates (start with p95 target=250ms).
- Instrument production to measure real-time KV hit rate and cold-start counters, add dashboard.
Medium-term (1-3 months):
- Pilot 8-bit quantized variant on 10% of traffic for short prompts; collect quality regressions via sampled human evals and automated evals.
- Implement hybrid routing: short-prompt small-model / long-prompt large-model.
- Update client-side guidance: truncate non-essential context and recommend token limits to app devs.
Operational playbook notes:
- On rollout, watch the p99 jump and error rates. Have automatic rollback thresholds: p95 > 400ms or error-rate > +0.5% absolute triggers rollback.
- Add a staged canary over 3 regions, ramp 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 48–72 hours.
